description: Format and collection settings of the story coverage ledger. A story-coverage.json sits beside the UI parts it covers and lists each exported part with its Stories, or with the reason it has none. This file says which files count as UI parts and what every entry must look like.

componentSourceExclusions.reason: Development-only sample, not a product UI component; the same Markdown renderer is covered by shared/markdown Stories.

collect.coverageFileNaming: story-coverage.json holds either one source (file) or several sources (files). A multi-source document is always named story-coverage.json; each entry in files may name its own owner, and otherwise uses the document owner. A single-source document may instead be named story-coverage.<name>.json, where <name> is its source file name without extension, when its folder already has a story-coverage.json. A source file belongs to one coverage document only.
collect.placement: A coverage file sits in the folder of the part it covers. Each Story ID it lists must be registered by a *.stories.tsx file in that same folder, so the Story and its coverage travel together.

entry.storyIdRule: Storybook's own ID: toId(meta.title, storyNameFromExport(exportName)) from storybook/internal/csf
entry.ownerRule: The owner is the unit that the planning inventory (UI-INVENTORY) assigns the source file to. That inventory lives outside this repository, so the check validates only the format.

inventory.method: The final unit uses the TypeScript compiler API to discover named PascalCase React component exports in TSX sources under collect.uiLayers. Every discovered export is present in a neighboring coverage ledger with registered Story IDs or a reasoned exclusion. app/development/MarkdownSample.tsx is explicitly excluded as a development-only sample. Non-visual APIs, hooks, models, and type-only exports remain covered by focused tests or the Stories of their owning component.

completeness.gate: Run pnpm --dir web build-storybook, pnpm --dir web verify:story-coverage, and pnpm --dir web test:storybook. The export verifier checks every exported React component found by the TypeScript compiler API and compares ledger IDs with the generated Storybook index in both directions; the Storybook support tests validate ledger placement and entry shape.
completeness.nodeCheckLimit: The export verifier recognizes named PascalCase value exports in TSX files containing JSX, plus named default component functions. It does not require Stories for API/model/hooks/types that do not render UI. Coverage test validation still checks every listed export and every Story ID.

storyOwnership.seed: U1 wrote the first Stories and coverage files of the representative parts, as seeds.
storyOwnership.after: From then on, the unit that the planning inventory (UI-INVENTORY) assigns to the source file extends the adjacent *.stories.tsx and story-coverage files. A unit must not add a second Story for a part that already has one. It edits the existing file.
storyOwnership.u1Scope: Shared support, dependencies and configuration under web/.storybook/ stay with U1.
